extracted.intended_audience: news executives, journalists, media researchers, funders and policymakers interested in public trust in news
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative framework and survey-based criteria for measuring public trust in local vs. national news organizations, including performance roles, topic-specific coverage trust, journalist attributes, and how ideology and labeling affect trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get the facts right (accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust that a news organization 'gets the facts right' — accuracy of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey shows majorities of Republicans and independents trust local news more than national news on accuracy; Democrats tend to trust national news more on this dimension. Accuracy is highlighted as a key indicator driving overall media trust (see Knight Foundation indicators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report the news without bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceived ability of news organizations to report news without political or ideological bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-thirds of Republicans and independents say local news is more accurate, balanced and unbiased. Democrats are more likely to trust national news to report without bias on several dimensions. Perception of bias strongly influences trust and can erode a local news advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give adequate attention to all sides of an issue (balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether coverage gives adequate attention to multiple sides or perspectives on an issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents rated local vs national on balance; partisan differences exist (Republicans/independents favor local). Balance is one of the critical indicators linked to overall trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give enough attention to the most important issues (agenda/prioritization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the organization gives sufficient attention to the topics the public considers most important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People very attentive to local news are more likely to trust local outlets to give enough attention to important issues (59% vs. 49%). Democrats tend to trust national news more on this dimension; partisan splits drive trust gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on different ways that problems can be solved (solutions reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that presents multiple solutions or approaches to addressing problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over two-thirds of Republicans and independents trust local news more than national on this. Respondents with higher local-news attention also rate local outlets higher on reporting different ways problems can be solved (68% vs. 56%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present high-quality, professional broadcasts/newspapers/websites (production quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception of professional production values and overall presentation quality across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one dimension where Democrats more often trust national outlets. The survey lists 'present high-quality, professional broadcasts, newspapers or websites' as a distinct performance role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give information you can use in your daily life (usefulness/relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether coverage provides practical, usable information for daily life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was the only dimension where Democrats trusted local more than national. Practical local coverage (e.g., weather, local services) can increase trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly identify editorials, commentaries or advertisements (transparency/labeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear separation and labeling of opinion/commentary and advertising from news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to distinguish journalism from commentary/ads is an explicit survey dimension; Democrats and others differ in which level of news they trust more on this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: local environment and weather emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in coverage of local environment issues and weather emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highest local trust among topics (75% 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot'). Local outlets are seen as especially trusted for immediate, place-based issues like weather and environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: environment and natural disasters (national level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in national news coverage of environment and natural disasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the only issue where nearly half (47%) say they have high trust in national news coverage—contrasting with strong local trust for local environment/weather emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: public health and safety (local)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in local outlets to cover public health and safety in respondents' local area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 58% rate local coverage highly; topic-level trust varies by age, partisan groups, and attention to local news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: public health and safety (national/U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in national outlets to cover public health and safety in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust in national coverage of U.S. public health/safety is lower than local equivalents for some respondents; patterns differ across party and demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: schools and education (local)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in local coverage of K-12 education in the local area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 52% trust local coverage highly; local trust on schools often outpaces national coverage on the same topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: schools and education (national/U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in national coverage of schools and education in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National coverage typically draws lower 'a great deal/quite a lot' trust than local coverage for schools; demographic and partisan splits apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: business and the economy (local)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in local coverage of business and the economy in respondents' local area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 51% trust local coverage highly; local business coverage is one area where partisan differences are smaller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: business and the economy (national/U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in national coverage of business and the U.S. economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National trust levels for economic coverage are generally lower than local equivalents for place-based economic reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: local politics and government
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in local news coverage of local politics and government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 45% 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' trust local coverage of local politics; those perceiving a large ideological gap with local media express very low trust (24%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: national politics and government
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in national news coverage of national politics and government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 36% express high trust; both local and national political coverage are among the least-trusted topics and are highly politicized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific trust: social and cultural issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in coverage of social/cultural issues (e.g., abortion, race relations, gun rights, LGBT rights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only about a third express high trust in both local and national coverage of these politicized topics; younger adults show particularly low trust in local coverage of social/cultural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: trustworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that journalists are trustworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local journalists have a comparative advantage on trustworthiness, though many respondents say the attribute applies to both local and national journalists; Republicans more likely to favor local when forced to choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that journalists are accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority think this applies to both local and national journalists (54%); local journalists get a modest comparative edge for some groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: neutral or unbiased
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that journalists are neutral or unbiased in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pluralities say this applies to both; local advantage exists for some respondents, but partisan splits affect evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: caring
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that journalists care about community and subjects they cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local journalists are rated higher on 'caring' by sizable pluralities; however many still say the attribute applies to both or neither.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: professional
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that journalists are professional in conduct and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majorities (about 60%) believe both local and national journalists are professional; views vary modestly by party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: informed about subjects they report on
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether journalists are knowledgeable about the beats they cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority (58%) think both local and national journalists are informed; local journalists are viewed slightly more informed by some respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: passionate
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that journalists are passionate about their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most respondents rate both local and national journalists as passionate; local advantage exists but is not overwhelming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist attribute: good communicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that journalists communicate clearly and effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Largest agreement applies to both local and national journalists (65%); small differences between local and national.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived ideological moderation of local news
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether local news is perceived as moderate, too liberal, or too conservative relative to national news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority describe local news as 'about right' (53%); perceptions of moderation contribute to higher local trust but are fragile—perceived ideological shifts reduce trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideological alignment between audience and local media
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of perceived ideological gap between an individual's views and the perceived political leanings of local media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 44% perceive little/no gap; 22% see a large gap. Those perceiving a large gap express much lower trust in local coverage, especially on politics and social issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived change in local news ideology over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether respondents think local news ideology has moved (more liberal/conservative) compared to five years ago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 51% say no change, 37% see more liberal, 11% more conservative. Those who perceive a shift are far less trusting of local news (31% vs. 55% who see no change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of labeling a story as local vs. national (source cue effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether identifying a story as from a local vs. national source changes trust in the same content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental results: respondents rated identical stories modestly more trustworthy when labeled local (average 2.5 vs 2.7 on a 5-point scale; 0.22 point advantage in a second experiment). The effect is small but statistically significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of partisan alignment of content with reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact on trust when article content aligns with the reader's partisan beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partisan alignment had a much larger effect than local labeling: aligned partisan content improved trust ratings by 0.92 points on the five-point scale, far exceeding the local vs national labeling effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to local news (audience engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the level of attention an individual pays to local news correlates with trust in local news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those very attentive to local news are more likely to trust local outlets on several dimensions (e.g., giving enough attention to important issues, reporting solutions). Higher engagement predicts higher trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place-based institutional confidence (contextual trust comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public confidence in local news relative to other local institutions (libraries, businesses, law enforcement, churches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local news ranks below some community institutions in public confidence (local libraries, local businesses), indicating that local news' trust should be assessed in the context of other trusted local institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability of local trust to perceived political bias or reduced coverage breadth/depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk that local news' trust advantage will erode if perceived ideological bias increases or breadth/depth of local coverage declines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report warns that local news' current trust advantage is fragile: increased perceptions of bias (63% of Republicans, 51% of independents perceive greater ideological bias) could cause trust to dissipate.
